title: TRL 1 — Basic principles observed
content: Scientific research has begun to be translated into applied research and development. Activity is limited to paper studies of a technology's basic properties, with no experimental proof. For a startup, this looks like a documented technical idea or literature review with no code, no prototype, and no laboratory result — the concept is described but nothing has been built or tested.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 2 — Technology concept formulated
content: Once basic principles are observed, practical applications can be speculated upon, but they remain analytic; no experimental proof or detailed analysis yet supports the invention. For a startup, this looks like a named product concept and an architecture sketch describing how the underlying principle would solve a specific problem, backed by rough back-of-envelope reasoning rather than any built code or lab result.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 3 — Experimental proof of concept
content: Active research and development is initiated, including analytical and laboratory studies to physically validate the analytical predictions of separate elements of the technology. For a startup, this means a scoped experiment or a proof-of-concept script has produced a recorded result showing the core mechanism functions in isolation, even though no components have been integrated into a working prototype.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 4 — Technology validated in laboratory
content: The basic technological components are integrated to establish that they work together, though the assembly is low-fidelity compared to the eventual system. A startup at this level has an integrated prototype exercised against synthetic or internal test data in a controlled setting, producing measured results, but it has not yet been exposed to real users, real data, or the target operating environment.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 5 — Technology validated in relevant environment
content: Fidelity of the integrated components increases significantly, and the basic technological components are combined with reasonably realistic supporting elements so the technology can be tested in a simulated environment. For a startup, this means the prototype runs against real customer data or in a staging environment that mirrors production, with results measured under near-real conditions even though it has not yet gone live for actual users.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 6 — Technology demonstrated in relevant environment
content: A representative model or prototype system, well beyond the level tested for TRL 5, is tested in a relevant environment, going beyond laboratory testing to simulated operational conditions. A startup at this level has run a pilot with a small number of real customers in their own environment, delivering an end-to-end result and capturing structured feedback, though the deployment is limited in scale and duration.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 7 — System prototype demonstration in operational environment
content: A prototype implementation, near or at the scale of the planned operational system, is demonstrated in an actual operational environment. For a startup, this looks like a substantially complete version of the product running live for real customers under actual operating conditions, in a limited rollout rather than a full launch, with monitoring in place to capture how it behaves outside a controlled trial.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 8 — System complete and qualified
content: The technology has been proven to work in its final form and under the expected range of conditions; in most cases this represents the end of true system development, with only minor refinements remaining. A startup here has completed functional, performance, security, and compliance testing against production requirements and is qualified for full launch, even though it has not yet accumulated a sustained operating track record.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: TRL 9 — Actual system proven in operational environment
content: The technology is in its final form and has been proven through successful operation under real mission conditions. For a startup, this means the product runs in production for real customers at expected load, with monitoring, incident response, and a track record of sustained operation rather than a pilot window. Remaining work is maintenance and iteration, not proving the system works.
citation: European Commission, Horizon Europe Work Programme, General Annex B — Technology Readiness Levels (TRL); consistent with ISO 16290:2013

title: MRL 1 — Market assumed, no buyer contact
content: The market is assumed rather than investigated: the team has a hypothesis about who would buy the product and why, but has not spoken with a single prospective buyer. Evidence at this level is limited to an internal one-pager describing the assumed customer and problem, with no external validation of any kind.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 2 — Target segment identified via secondary research
content: A target market segment has been named and described using secondary sources — industry reports, competitor research, published market sizing — but the team still has not had a single conversation with a real prospective buyer. Evidence is a desk-research document identifying the segment and its estimated size, not any direct signal from the market itself.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 3 — Informal problem interviews
content: The team has held informal conversations with prospective buyers — problem interviews or casual conversations at events — surfacing anecdotal interest, but no prospect has made any commitment. Evidence is a set of interview notes or call logs showing a handful of conversations, with reactions recorded but no willingness-to-pay signal.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 4 — Structured customer discovery
content: Customer discovery has been formalized: structured interviews have been run across multiple prospects using a consistent script, and a common pain point has been validated across that sample. Evidence is a discovery report summarizing interview themes across a named number of prospects, though no prospect has yet indicated a specific willingness to pay.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 5 — Paid pilots with named customers
content: Demand has moved from stated interest to a financial commitment: the startup has run repeated paid pilots with named customers, each willing to pay for a defined trial period. Evidence is signed pilot agreements or purchase orders from more than one named customer, together with pilot usage or outcome data collected during the engagement.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 6 — Repeat sales beyond initial pilots
content: The customer base has expanded beyond the original pilots — additional paying customers have been acquired using a pitch or process that is starting to repeat — but there is no scalable acquisition channel yet and each sale still depends heavily on founder involvement. Evidence is a growing list of paying customers with dates of acquisition, plus early renewal or expansion revenue from at least one pilot customer.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 7 — Predictable pipeline and renewals
content: A defined ideal customer profile and at least one acquisition channel now produce a predictable pipeline, with multiple customers renewing rather than churning after their initial term. Evidence is a documented ICP, a named acquisition channel with a measured conversion rate, and renewal records from more than one customer cohort.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 8 — Repeatable playbook, forecast variance narrowing
content: Sales are handled by more than the founders and a repeatable playbook exists across several customer segments or channels, but forecasts still carry meaningful variance and are not yet reliable predictors of actual revenue. Evidence is a documented sales playbook in use by a non-founder seller, revenue data across multiple segments, and a forecast-versus-actual comparison showing that variance.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: MRL 9 — Repeatable sales motion, predictable conversion and retention
content: The business runs a repeatable sales motion with predictable conversion rates and measured retention, and revenue forecasts have proven accurate over multiple consecutive periods. Evidence is a documented conversion rate tracked across several sales cycles, a churn or retention figure benchmarked over time, and forecast accuracy demonstrated against actual closed revenue.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 1 — No regulatory analysis
content: No analysis has been done of which laws, regulations, or licensing regimes apply to the product or its operation; the regulatory landscape is entirely unknown to the team. Evidence at this level is the absence of any regulatory review — no memo, no advisor engaged, no list of candidate rules.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 2 — Regulatory domain identified
content: The team has identified which regulatory domain and which oversight body plausibly governs the product — for example, data protection, financial services, or medical device rules — but has not obtained any formal legal assessment of what specifically applies. Evidence is an internal note naming the likely regulator or regulatory area, based on the team's own research rather than counsel.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 3 — Counsel engaged, preliminary opinion
content: External legal or regulatory counsel has been engaged to map the applicable rules, and a preliminary opinion on requirements has been received, but no application or filing process has started. Evidence is an engagement letter or memo from counsel setting out the requirements the product is expected to need to satisfy.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 4 — Requirements checklist documented
content: The specific permits, licenses, or certifications required have been identified and documented as a checklist against named standards, so the team knows exactly what must be obtained even though nothing has yet been submitted. Evidence is a requirements checklist naming each permit or certification and the standard it must meet.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 5 — Permit applications lodged
content: The applicable permits and licenses have been identified and applications for them have actually been lodged with the relevant authority, moving the startup from planning into the regulatory process itself. Evidence is a submission receipt or application reference number from the regulator for at least one required permit.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 6 — Partial or conditional approval
content: At least one of the identified permits or certifications has been granted, or a conditional approval has been received, while the remaining requirements are still pending with the regulator. Evidence is a granted certificate or conditional-approval letter for part of the requirement set, alongside open applications for the rest.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 7 — Provisional license under supervision
content: A full application is under active review with the regulator, information requests from the regulator have been answered, and a provisional or pilot license has been granted that allows limited real-world operation under supervision. Evidence is correspondence showing responses to regulator information requests and a provisional license document with its stated conditions.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 8 — Full compliance, internal processes running
content: Full compliance has been achieved for every requirement identified at the outset, and internal compliance processes — standard operating procedures, an audit trail, a responsible owner — are documented and running, even though no external audit has yet confirmed them. Evidence is signed-off internal SOPs and a compliance log covering each identified requirement.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: RRL 9 — Fully compliant and externally audited
content: The startup is fully compliant and has passed an external audit, and the ongoing obligations that compliance requires — renewals, reporting, monitoring — are resourced with a named owner and a tracked calendar. Evidence is a signed external audit report and a renewal or reporting calendar with an assigned compliance owner.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 1 — Adoption assumed
content: Adoption is assumed rather than observed: the team believes users will want the product but no user has interacted with it in any form. Evidence is limited to an internal persona description with no demo, no mockup review, and no recorded user reaction.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 2 — Adoption hypothesis documented
content: An adoption hypothesis has been written down, naming a specific target user persona and the behavior change expected of them, but no member of that persona group has yet seen the product in any form. Evidence is a documented persona and adoption hypothesis, with no demo or user session on record.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 3 — Informal demo reactions
content: The product concept has been shown to a handful of prospective users through informal demos, and their verbal reactions have been captured, but no behavior has actually been measured — reactions are qualitative impressions only. Evidence is a log of demo sessions with recorded verbal feedback from a small number of people.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 4 — Structured usability testing
content: Structured usability or concept-testing sessions have been run with prospective users, collecting task-completion and satisfaction data, but every interaction has occurred under direct observation rather than independent use. Evidence is a usability test report with task-completion rates and satisfaction scores from a defined set of observed sessions.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 5 — Measured usage by trial users
content: Real users beyond the founding team have used the product independently in a trial, and their usage has actually been measured rather than merely observed. Evidence is trial usage data — session logs, feature-usage counts, or completion events — captured from named non-founder users without the founders present.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 6 — Repeat usage and first referrals
content: The trial cohort has expanded and users are returning for repeat sessions rather than trying the product once, with engagement metrics such as return rate now tracked, and the first organic, unprompted referrals from users to their peers have begun to appear. Evidence is a return-rate metric across a named trial cohort plus at least one documented organic referral.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 7 — Sustained engagement, retention tracked
content: A defined cohort of active users is engaging with the product on a sustained, week-over-week basis, and the team is tracking a retention curve over a meaningful period such as ninety days rather than a single trial window. Evidence is a retention curve chart for a named cohort covering at least ninety days of activity.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 8 — Unincentivized retention, early advocacy
content: Users continue using the product without ongoing incentives or founder intervention prompting them to do so, and early advocacy signals — referrals, testimonials, unsolicited case-study requests — are starting to appear on their own. Evidence is usage data showing continuation after incentives were withdrawn plus a small number of unprompted testimonials or referrals.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ARL 9 — Sustained voluntary adoption with measured advocacy
content: Adoption is sustained and voluntary across multiple user cohorts, with retention benchmarked over an extended period and advocacy quantified through metrics such as a Net Promoter Score or referral rate, all without ongoing incentives driving the behavior. Evidence is multi-cohort retention data over an extended period alongside a tracked NPS or referral-rate figure.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 1 — Founders only, no defined roles
content: The venture consists of its founders only, and no roles, responsibilities, or decision rights have been formally defined among them — everyone does everything as needed. Evidence is the absence of any org chart, written role description, or documented decision process.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 2 — Informal division of responsibilities
content: Founders have informally divided responsibilities between themselves based on skill or interest, but nothing is written down and decisions are still made ad hoc rather than through any agreed process. Evidence is, at most, an informal verbal understanding of who handles what, with no written role description or org chart.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 3 — First non-founder contributor
content: A first contributor beyond the founders — a contractor, advisor, or part-time hire — has joined the venture, but there is still no formal governance structure or documented operating process guiding how work happens. Evidence is a contract or engagement letter for the first non-founder contributor, with no accompanying process documentation.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 4 — Initial role definitions and processes
content: Initial role definitions have been drafted for the core team and the first process documentation exists — an onboarding guide, a basic decision log — and the venture is actively considering or has made its first full-time hire beyond the founders. Evidence is a written role-definition document and at least one basic process artifact such as an onboarding checklist.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 5 — Defined roles and basic governance
content: The organization has defined roles across an org chart, a basic governance mechanism such as regular advisor or board check-ins is in place, and specific key hires needed for the next stage have been identified by name or role. Evidence is a written org chart, a recurring governance meeting on the calendar, and a hiring plan naming the next key roles.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 6 — Key functional hires onboarded
content: Key functional hires — a first engineering lead, a first sales hire — have been onboarded with documented responsibilities, and basic operational policies such as a compensation framework and an onboarding process now exist for the wider team. Evidence is signed offer letters for named functional leads plus a written compensation or onboarding policy document.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 7 — Multiple teams, management cadence
content: Multiple functional teams now operate under named team leads, escalation and reporting lines are documented, and a regular management cadence — a weekly leadership sync tracked against OKRs — is running. Evidence is an org chart showing multiple teams with leads, a documented escalation path, and OKR tracking records from recurring leadership meetings.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 8 — Formal governance body established
content: A formal governance body — a board including independent members, or an equivalent oversight structure — has been established, and core operational functions such as finance, HR, and compliance are run by dedicated staff rather than the founders themselves. Evidence is board meeting minutes showing independent members and organizational charts showing dedicated finance, HR, or compliance staff.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: ORL 9 — Staffed functions sustaining scale
content: The organization is staffed across all core functions with documented processes and succession plans, and governance operates independently enough of founder day-to-day involvement to sustain further scale. Evidence is a full leadership roster with named successors, audited process documentation across finance, HR, and operations, and board minutes showing governance decisions made without founder direction.
citation: Balanced Readiness Level assessment (BRLa), Technological Forecasting and Social Change (2021) — dimension framework; level descriptors authored against its stated criteria

title: IRL 1 — No funding plan, founder time only
content: No funding plan exists at all: the venture is running on founder time and personal resources with no target raise amount, no use-of-funds outline, and no investor contact of any kind. Evidence is simply the absence of any funding document or investor conversation.

title: IRL 2 — Informal funding hypothesis
content: An informal funding hypothesis has been noted — a general sense that a seed round will eventually be needed — but no target amount, use-of-funds outline, or investor list has been drafted. Evidence is, at most, a passing mention in founder notes rather than any funding document.

title: IRL 3 — Funding plan drafted
content: A funding plan has been drafted specifying a target raise amount and a rough use-of-funds breakdown, though the team has not yet held a single conversation with a potential investor. Evidence is a written funding plan document with a stated amount and a use-of-funds sketch.

title: IRL 4 — Initial investor conversations
content: Initial investor conversations have taken place — warm-intro meetings or angel-network pitches — using a one-pager or deck, but no term sheet, commitment, or signed instrument has resulted from them. Evidence is a pitch deck circulated to named investors and a log of meetings held, with no signed agreement yet.

title: IRL 5 — Grant or angel funding secured
content: Grant or angel funding has actually been secured, backed by a documented use of funds mapped to specific milestones the money is meant to buy. Evidence is a signed grant award letter or angel or SAFE agreement together with a budget document tying the funds to named milestones.

title: IRL 6 — Funds deployed, burn tracked
content: The funds secured in the prior stage have been substantially deployed against their stated milestones, and for the first time the venture tracks basic financial reporting such as monthly burn rate and runway. Evidence is a monthly burn or runway report and evidence of spend against the previously stated milestones.

title: IRL 7 — Institutional round in process
content: A formal institutional seed round is underway — term sheet negotiations are active or a lead investor has been identified — and due diligence materials have been prepared and shared. Evidence is a data room or diligence package shared with a named prospective lead investor and any term sheet drafts under discussion.

title: IRL 8 — Round closed, governance not yet active
content: An institutional round has closed at the term-sheet stage, with signed financing documents and funds transferred into the company's accounts, but the reporting cadence and governance structures that typically accompany institutional capital — a board seat, regular investor updates — are not yet operating. Evidence is signed closing documents and a bank record of funds received, with no investor-reporting cadence yet established.

title: IRL 9 — Institutional round with reporting and governance
content: An institutional round has closed and the reporting and governance that come with it are actually operating: funds are deployed, investors receive regular financial reporting, and formal governance — a board seat, information rights — is active. Evidence is a recurring investor-update cadence, financial statements shared on schedule, and board-meeting records showing an investor board seat in use.
